question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Velocity Vector of a Particle Moving in Two Dimensions at a Given Time
question.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\sqrt{4t+1},3t-2⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v$ at time $t=2.$
question.worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{4t+1}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{\sqrt{4t+1}},3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=2,$ we substitute into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =⟨\frac{2}{\sqrt{4(2)+1}},3⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{\sqrt{9}},3⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},3⟩\end{aligned}
$$
